name: Busco
description: Assess genome assembly and annotation completeness

inputs.name: input
inputs.label: Sequences to analyse
inputs.help: Can be an assembled genome or transcriptome (DNA), or protein sequences from an annotated gene set.

test_parameter.name: use_augustus_selector
test_parameter.label: Select a gene predictor
test_parameter.help: In the case of a prokaryotic genome, Prodigal is the default gene predictor

options.label: Use the default species for selected lineage

parameters.name: augustus_species
parameters.label: Augustus species model
parameters.help: If model name is different than species name it is shown in parentheses.

parameters.name: long
parameters.label: Optimization mode Augustus self-training
parameters.help: Adds considerably to run time, but can improve results for some non-model organisms

test_parameter.name: lineage_mode
test_parameter.label: Auto-detect or select lineage?
test_parameter.help: Let BUSCO decide the best lineage automatically, or select from known lineage

parameters.name: auto_lineage
parameters.label: auto-lineage group
parameters.help: Taxonomic group to run with auto-lineage.

parameters.name: generic_results
parameters.label: Do you want to display the results from the generic lineage
parameters.help: BUSCO generates files for the parent lineage (generic) and the final selected lineage (specific). Generally, the lineage to select for your assessments should be the most specific lineage available. The generic lineage datasets for the domains archaea, bacteria and eukaryota.

inputs.name: plot_percentages
inputs.label: lot the percentages of BUSCOs instead of the number of BUSCOs
inputs.help: Only relevant for summary image output

parameters.name: limit
parameters.label: How many candidate regions to consider

parameters.name: contig_break
parameters.label: Number of contiguous Ns to signify a break between contigs

help.content:
BUSCO: Assessing genome assembly and annotation completeness with Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Interpreting the results
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

BUSCO_ attempts to provide a quantitative assessment of the completeness in terms of the expected gene content of a
genome assembly, transcriptome, or annotated gene set. The results are simplified into categories of Complete
and single-copy, Complete and duplicated, Fragmented, or Missing BUSCOs.

BUSCO completeness results make sense only in the context of the biology of your organism.
You have to understand whether missing or duplicated genes are of biological or technical origin.
For instance, a high level of duplication may be explained by a recent whole duplication event
(biological) or a chimeric assembly of haplotypes (technical).
Transcriptomes and protein sets that are not filtered for isoforms will lead to a high proportion of duplicates.
Therefore you should filter them before a BUSCO analysis.
Finally, focusing on specific tissues or specific life stages and conditions in a transcriptomic experiment
is unlikely to produce a BUSCO-complete transcriptome. In this case, consistency across your samples
is what you will be aiming for.

For more information please refer to the Busco_ `user guide <https://busco.ezlab.org /busco_userguide.html#interpreting-the-results>`_
.

.. _BUSCO: http://busco.ezlab.org/
